headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt-injection, leakage, and write-conflict pathways plausible; no direct sandbox evidence reduces confidence.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads files from the filesystem and uses stdin/stdout, while cognee processes documents and workflows with session memory. Because Mentat can consume file content and cognee can generate content from documents, a shared-file bridge could let attacker-controlled text influence Mentat. No MCP or clipboard bridge is documented, so this is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or exported files, injected instructions in those files can reach Mentat.
IF cognee outputs are copied into files that Mentat later reads, prompt injection becomes feasible.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different directories.
Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted documents into cognee.
Review file contents before passing them to Mentat.
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee touches personal data, finance data, and support history, while Mentat reads and writes filesystem content and has broad network egress to a model provider. If they share a workspace, sensitive material can flow from cognee-managed files into Mentat and onward to a third party. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary, so the leakage path is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF cognee stores sensitive records in files that Mentat can read, those records may be exposed to Mentat's model provider.
IF both agents operate in the same directory tree, file contents can cross from cognee to Mentat without explicit export controls.
mitigations: Keep sensitive cognee data outside Mentat's workspace.
Use separate OS users or containers.
Restrict Mentat to redacted files only.
Rotate and scope model-provider keys narrowly.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, and cognee supports multiple instances with agentic user/tenant isolation but no explicit locking. If both touch the same repo or workspace, concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt git state. The shared-state-via-filesystem model on Mentat makes this a default write-conflict risk.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same git repository, conflicting writes can occur.
IF cognee materializes outputs into files that Mentat also edits, last-writer-wins corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working tree.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Commit or snapshot before handoff.
Use git locks or a single-writer policy.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level coordination primitives.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat is a coding assistant that proposes diffs, and cognee produces documents, decisions, and workflows. If Mentat treats cognee-generated outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect code changes or workflow edits. The profiles do not show a verification gate between them, but Mentat's diff-based edit proposals reduce immediate blast radius versus autonomous execution.
conditions: IF cognee outputs are fed directly into Mentat as task context, Mentat may propagate mistakes.
IF Mentat's proposed diffs are accepted without review, downstream errors can persist.
mitigations: Require human review of all diffs.
Cross-check cognee outputs against source data.
Insert a verification step before edits.
Limit Mentat to non-production branches.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while Mentat reads and writes local files and sends prompts to a configured model provider. If EU personal data or regulated records are placed into Mentat's workspace, they may leave the intended residency or retention boundary. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the mismatch is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in files that Mentat sends to a model provider, residency or retention obligations may be violated.
IF cognee and Mentat use different retention policies on the same records, compliance drift can occur.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from Mentat inputs.
Confirm provider-region settings before use.
Shorten retention on both systems.
Document a shared data-handling policy.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention enforcement.
